newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller attacks gov's plan hiking tuition.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller attacks gov's plan hiking tuition.

text.p: The New York State Comptroller on Wednesday attacked Gov George Pataki's plan to raise tuition for state university students while cutting aid, saying it was not the way to close a budget gap.

"Unfortunately, the governor looks at education as not an investment but as an expense. Even now, after the governor himself has identified new revenues totaling twice the amount of his proposed higher education cuts, he has not retracted them," said H. Carl McCall, in prepared remarks.
The state watchdog estimated that when added to a $750 tuition increase enacted last year, the new proposal for a $400 hike would equal an over 40 percent rise in two years.

Further, the Republican governor's plan to cut the Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) would deny grants to almost 38,000 students, McCall said, noting the average award would fall by $389 or 17 percent. "These cuts fall hardest on students from lower-income families," said the comptroller, a potential Democratic candidate for governor.
He pressed the legislature to restore Pataki's proposed cuts. The Democrat-led Assembly has opposed the governor's education cuts.
